newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Smith confirms deal to sell power stations.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Smith confirms deal to sell power stations.

text.p: New Zealand First has agreed to National's plan to sell off eight small hydro stations, Conservation Minister Nick Smith said on Monday.
He said the agreement would see the eight stations sold either to local supply companies, Maori iwi (tribal) interests, or a combination of the two, the New Zealand Press Association reported.

But a spokesman for New Zealand First leader and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters told Reuters that Peters would comment after he had talk to party negotiators who had handled that area of the coalition talks.

New Zealand First campaigned on a strong platform of opposing state asset sales. But its Maori members are seen likely to support the sale of the small hydro-stations, some of which are included in Treaty of Waitangi claims agreements, while others are being eyed by Maori for future claims.
Smith said the Government remained committed to keeping ownership of the major generating stations, but the eight small stations were better in local hands.

His comments followed newspaper reports quoting State-Owned Enterprises Minister Jenny Shipley as saying National and New Zealand First had reached a "clear understanding" on the sales during coalition talks.
The government originally announced its intention to sell the eight stations, which together make up nearly four percent of New Zealand's generation capacity, in mid-1995.

The eight stations are Matahina near Whakatane, the Coleridge and Highbank stations near Christchurch, Cobb near Nelson, the Kaitawa, Tuai and Piripaua stations near Lake Waikaremoana, and the Mangahao station near Levin.
